actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

facts.text: The README lists a steppable Gymnasium environment and faster-than-real-time, multi-instance simulation
The installation requires nvidia-driver, docker and nvidia-container-toolkit and builds the images with sim_build.sh
Installing aas-gym is pip3 install -e . from the aas-gym directory after the Installation steps
aas-gym describes itself as a Gymnasium wrapper for the aerial-autonomy-stack
aas-gym requires Python ^3.12 and depends on numpy ^2.4, gymnasium ^1.2, docker ^7.1 and pyzmq ^27.1
AASEnv is a Gymnasium environment class with render modes human and ansi
The action space is a one-element Box of floats from -1.0 to 1.0 with dtype float32
The observation space is a Box of the Gazebo /clock [seconds, nanoseconds] with low [0.0, 0.0] and high [inf, 1e9]
The constructor defaults are gym_freq_hz 50, an init duration of 80.0 s and a maximum episode length of 300.0 s
max_steps is int(MAX_EPISODE_LENGTH_SEC * GYM_FREQ_HZ), 15000 at the default 50 Hz
AASEnv creates the simulation container from the simulation-image:latest image
AASEnv creates one aircraft container from aircraft-image:latest per drone
reset restarts the simulation and aircraft containers, opens the ZeroMQ socket and sends the special action 9999.0 to reset the world
step reads force = action[0], sends it to the simulator and receives the clock in reply
Every step returns reward -1.0, terminated False, and truncated when step_count >= max_steps
The observation is np.array([sim_sec, sim_nanosec]) and info repeats them as sim_time_sec and sim_time_nanosec
reset passes seed only to gym.Env.reset, while the ZeroMQ reset payload is the constant 9999.0 and carries no seed
AASEnv-v0 is registered in gym_run.py with entry_point=AASEnv
The ZeroMQ bridge runs the world unpaused for init_duration seconds on reset and pauses it afterwards
The ZeroMQ bridge publishes the double action on /action and advances the paused world by step_size physics steps
The step target time is current_sim_time + step_size * physics_dt - 0.0001 s
The bridge computes step_size = physics_freq_hz / gym_freq_hz and physics_dt is 0.004 s for PX4, so with the default gym_freq_hz 50 one control step is nominally 20 ms

determinism.notes: reset(seed) forwards the seed to gym.Env's generator (aas_env.py:291), but the simulator reset is the constant 9999.0 payload (aas_env.py:327-328) and the fake ignores the seed, so no seed reproduces a trajectory

gaps: the checked fake models only the simulated clock and the constant -1 step reward: there is no Gazebo/PX4 rigid-body dynamics, contact, actuator, sensor, wind, camera or LiDAR model, and the real Dockerized simulation was not run
the clock start, the 80 s reset run and the control period in the fake are test data that mirror the constructor defaults, not a calibrated model of a Gazebo world
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0 and only cap.world.step.v1 advances simulated time
the seed reaches only gym.Env's random generator and not the simulator, so determinism is none
snapshot and restore are not offered: AASEnv exposes no get_state/set_state
the observation is only the Gazebo /clock [seconds, nanoseconds]; the camera and LiDAR streams are not part of the observation space
the fake returns Python floats and lists; upstream returns float64 numpy arrays
the control period is nominal 1/gym_freq_hz; the ZeroMQ bridge targets step_size * physics_dt minus 0.1 ms, so the real clock increments can differ

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
